findings.title: basedOn.pttV9.fx5Intent silently drops 62% of the live v9 FX-5 intent, including one assert and one honesty statement that survive nowhere else in the artifact
findings.measured: Live v9's FX-5 intent is 543 characters. The subject's fx5Intent is 208 — a true prefix, cut at a sentence boundary, with no ellipsis or truncation marker. 335 characters (62%) are dropped.
findings.droppedTail: For each, assert the deterministic outcome named in raceSemantics, assert no post-revocation commit record exists, and assert cleanup closed within its declared bound. The split label is not hedging: the fixture genuinely enforces that the HOST commits nothing after r, and genuinely cannot speak to what the component did on its own.

whatSurvivesElsewhere.assertNoPostRevocationCommitRecord: PARTIALLY. 'post-revocation commit record' occurs once, as a whatIsNotAuthored line, and each state carries commitRecord NOT-AUTHORED. Present as a not-authored item rather than as an assert.
whatSurvivesElsewhere.assertCleanupClosedWithinDeclaredBound: PARTIALLY. 'cleanup-bound' occurs five times across authorityClaim, purpose, whatIsAuthored, whatIsNotAuthored and doesNot — but only as the number that is not authored. 'cleanup closed' 0 and 'declared bound' 0, so the requirement itself is not recorded.
whatSurvivesElsewhere.assertDeterministicOutcomeNamedInRaceSem: NOT AT ALL. 'raceSemantics' 0, 'race' 0, 'deterministic' 0. This assert vanishes from the artifact entirely.
whatSurvivesElsewhere.theSplitLabelHonestyStatement: NOT AT ALL. 'split label' 0, 'ambient' 0, 'component did' 0. v9's own statement of what FX-5 can and cannot prove is absent, as is FX-5's proves field ('ENFORCEMENT of the host's own commit path; DISCLOSURE with respect to ambient authority'), which the subject does not carry.

findings.whyThisIsASHOULDFIXAndNotAnObservation: This reviewer graded a structurally similar truncation on doctor-fc-ro-input-corpus.v1 as an OBSERVATION earlier in this session, for three stated reasons. Applying the same three tests here, two fail. (1) FC-RO: the dropped pass property was carried near-verbatim elsewhere in the artifact. HERE: one dropped assert and the entire honesty statement survive nowhere at all. (2) FC-RO: the string was a true prefix, so nothing false was asserted. HERE: this test still HOLDS — the quotation asserts nothing v9 does not say. (3) FC-RO: the field the artifact's authority rested on, fcRoExactByteIntent, was character-for-character exact, and the truncated field was a secondary variantsVerbatim list. HERE: fx5Intent IS the artifact's only source quotation; there is no exact field behind it.
findings.whyItIsNotAHouseConvention: The immediately preceding sibling in the same series, cited by this subject at fb5783e0 and authored 96 seconds earlier, carries fx4Intent character-for-character EQUAL to live v9 and additionally carries v9's five asserts on every one of its 32 states as assertsNamedNotAuthored. FX-5 carries a 38% prefix and no asserts field on any state. A reader comparing the two siblings would reasonably conclude FX-5 simply has no asserts, which is false.
findings.consequence: A later fixture author or coordinator reading fx5Intent as the record of the source pin would learn that FX-5 requires four positions and nothing more. They would not learn that a deterministic outcome must be asserted per position against raceSemantics, nor that v9 expressly disclaims what the fixture can say about the component's own behaviour. The aggravating detail is that the dropped sentence is also where v9 states the cleanup-bound requirement — so the artifact honours this review's cleanup-bound prohibition while concealing where that requirement comes from.
findings.fix: Restore fx5Intent to the full 543-character live value, or mark the truncation explicitly and carry the three asserts as the FX-4 sibling does. Either repair is mechanical and changes no authored state.
findings.notTheFix: Nothing prohibited was authored and no custody check failed. This finding is about fidelity of the source record, not about the four positions, which are correct.

decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record as-is. The substance is sound and should be kept verbatim: the four positions are exactly v9's four, each a true substring of the live intent, and every prohibition in the dispatch is respected — no journal bytes, no envelope, and no cleanup-bound number, with a bare-integer set of only 0, 03, 1 and 26. A v2 that restores basedOn.pttV9.fx5Intent to the full 543-character live value — or marks the truncation and carries the three asserts as the FX-4 sibling does — would, on these bytes, carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: Everything in this artifact verifies except one thing, and that one thing is the field the whole artifact rests on. fx5Intent is not equal to live v9's FX-5 intent: it is a true prefix keeping 208 of 543 characters, cut at a sentence boundary with no ellipsis, dropping 62%. I then located each dropped element and searched for it elsewhere in the artifact rather than assuming. Two survive partially — 'no post-revocation commit record' as a whatIsNotAuthored line plus commitRecord NOT-AUTHORED per state, and the cleanup bound only as the number that is not authored, with 'cleanup closed' and 'declared bound' both at zero. Two survive not at all: 'assert the deterministic outcome named in raceSemantics' is gone entirely, with raceSemantics, race and deterministic all at zero occurrences; and so is v9's split-label sentence, its own honesty statement that the fixture 'genuinely enforces that the HOST commits nothing after r, and genuinely cannot speak to what the component did on its own'. The subject also omits v9's proves field, which is the label that sentence exists to gloss, so the DISCLOSURE half of this class is absent from the artifact altogether. I graded a structurally similar truncation on doctor-fc-ro-input-corpus.v1 as an observation earlier today, and I want you to see the standard is stable rather than arbitrary, so the finding states the three reasons that saved FC-RO and applies them here: the dropped material survived elsewhere there but does not here; the prefix asserts nothing false, which still holds; and there the truncated field was a secondary list while the artifact's primary quotation was exact, whereas here fx5Intent is the only source quotation there is. Two of three fail. Nor is it a house convention: the sibling this subject itself cites at fb5783e0, authored 96 seconds earlier, carries fx4Intent character-for-character EQUAL to live and carries v9's five asserts on all 32 of its states. FX-5 carries a 38% prefix and no asserts field at all, so a reader comparing them would reasonably conclude FX-5 has no asserts. The aggravating detail is that the dropped sentence is also where v9 states 'assert cleanup closed within its declared bound' — this review's own prohibition — so the artifact honours the prohibition while concealing where the requirement comes from. Everything else is clean and worth keeping. The four positions are exactly v9's four, each verified as a true substring of the live intent, none added or dropped. The cleanup-bound sweep is decisive: bare integers are only 0, 03, 1 and 26, where 03 is v9's own file-03 reference inside the quotation, and 'seconds', 'ms', 'timeout' and 'within' are all zero. The envelope probe is clean, with four state field names, no nested object and all four 'envelope' occurrences being negations. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at ea47fc7d and 0444 at both samplings, five of five cited digests equal live bytes, both cited standings confirmed at Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex verdict, the D-163 join confirms OBL-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true with owner none and FX-5 inside its fourteen, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, and SATISFIED and QUALIFIED occur zero times. Thirteen attacks run, twelve refuted, one landing. The fix is mechanical and changes no authored state.
